Hi WB,

Okay, they're not exactly typos but punctuation inconsistencies like en dash "–" in place of em dash "—" or using them both with spaces "word — word" and without spaces "word—word" — the style has to be consistent. I'd keep it "word — word" throughout. For eg., "Charlie Kirk – The Best and Greatest of Us" title on the web uses en dash "–" and not em dash "—", so it has to be "Charlie Kirk — The Best and Greatest of Us". Also, I'd add period at the end of complete sentences even in blurbs and points, which I find missing at many places, for e.g., "Family: Married to Jeanette Dousdebes Rubio since 1998; the couple has four children" — I hope it makes sense.

Points corresponding your feedback:

1\. The inconsistent empty spaces at the end of most articles is not only about the layout, font, images — it's more to do with the length of the content, because the articles were created for web and not for magazine editorial. The traditional or ideal way of addressing this issue is to add more text — because in magazine or newspaper editorial, word count is very crucial. The layout is always done using dummy text "Lorem Ipsum" based on the approximate word count per page that you get from the editorial team; and then you balance it with images and blurbs. After the layout is completed in terms of the pagination requirements, the editorial team works based on the word count of the dummy text. However, in case of pre-written articles, the author or the editorial team would cut short or add more text to match the word count. So, in our situation, I did what best could be done — to balance with images and even with text kerning. But, in order to achieve like "Confirmed Alien Existence Can’t Cast Doubt on Christianity' article" — we need to add more text, and/or images where possible. For example, for "Made in the USA: The Return of Domestic Manufacturing", we can add a big image on page 24 to cover up page 25 as much as possible — but for exact consistency, adding more text to match the word count is the only way ahead. Based on this criteria, you can send me more images wherever you think we can add in order to fill up the white space toward the end, as much as possible.

2\. This is an optimized version, besides the ads are not replaced yet with the PSD versions you sent — they'll all be fixed in the next version.

3\. If you're referring to the body font, then it's the same font that you've used on your website. However, please see attached 3 alternative options — I'd go with **Inter** font.

4\. I've sent you a spread version to give you a better idea of the layout. For Flip Book, we'll have to upload the pages version. The page count should be even, i.e., divisible by 2. Sure, I'll test it on <http://Hezine.com> once we're though with this.

For modern magazine layouts, a semi-condensed san serif font is highly recommended, especially when paired with a serif font for heading. Trust me, **INTER** font is much better in terms of thickness, legibility, spacing, and modern appeal.
